# Provenance log

Every non-trivial algorithm or design borrowed from outside the project. Format:

| Area | What | Source (paper / doc / repo + licence) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|

| Core / math | PCG32 random generator (XSH-RR, 64-bit state, `pcg32_srandom` seeding, unbiased bounded rejection) | [class: public-literature] Melissa E. O'Neill, "PCG: A Family of Simple Fast Space-Efficient Statistically Good Algorithms for Random Number Generation" (2014), pcg-random.org | Re-implemented; tested against the published pcg32 demo vectors (seed 42, stream 54) |
| Core / math | Frustum plane extraction from a view-projection matrix (clip z ∈ [0, w], reversed-Z aware) | [class: public-literature] Gribb & Hartmann, "Fast Extraction of Viewing Frustum Planes from the World-View-Projection Matrix" (2001) | Degenerate far plane of the reversed-Z infinite projection is dropped |
| Core / math | AABB transform by centre and extents | [class: public-literature] J. Arvo, "Transforming Axis-Aligned Bounding Boxes", Graphics Gems (1990) \| |  |
| Core / math | Ray/AABB slab test | [class: public-literature] Kay & Kajiya, "Ray Tracing Complex Scenes", SIGGRAPH 1986 \| |  |

Phase is packed in the fractional part of the emitter id. |
| VFX | Hue-preserving peak scale for HDR particle cores (`peak > 1` scales every channel by `1/peak`, so the hue is unchanged). The billboard writes premultiplied `rgb * alpha`. A pink core stays pink | `quality::tonemap_display`, `present.wgsl` `tonemap` |

The base colour is not recoloured | [class: public-literature] Masaki Kawase, "Frame Buffer Postprocessing Effects in DOUBLE-S.T.E.A.L", GDC 2003 (the small gather). This is one pass over the excess only, not that paper's multi-pass pyramid | `gpu/present.wgsl` `add_bloom`. Sky and ground stay at or below 1, so they do not bloom |
| VFX | Procedural sprite atlas (radial falloffs, FBM value noise for puff tile, noise-minus-radius puff silhouette, gaussian star, teardrop flame) | [class: public-literature] PCG32 random generator (O'Neill 2014) + value noise / fractional Brownian motion (Ken Perlin, "Improving Noise", SIGGRAPH 2002). The puff card is a density field `noise − radius`. The flare is a narrow gaussian core plus four exponential arms. The flame is a soft teardrop (tip up) with FBM holes and an equal-channel shade, so stacked cards read as a volume and the particle tint keeps its hue | Identity tiles 0..6, a 16-frame puff sheet (tiles 8..24) and an 8-frame flame sheet (tiles 24..32, `SpriteId::FireAnim`). Each frame shifts the FBM phase. Byte-stable across platforms. |
| VFX | Bitonic sort network for depth-ordering alpha-blended particles on GPU | [class: public-literature] K. E. Batcher, "Sorting Networks and their Applications", AFIPS 1968 | Standard bitonic merge in WGSL, indirect-draw driven. |
| VFX | Soft particles: depth-buffer fade to avoid hard particle/geometry intersections | [class: public-literature] Lorach, "Soft Particles" (NVIDIA DX10 whitepaper, 2007) | Implemented in WGSL fragment shader: fade = clamp((surface_depth − particle_depth) / softness_width). |
| VFX | Projected decals: box projection from the depth buffer, grazing-angle fade, edge fade; albedo atlas sampled as sRGB | [class: public-literature] Pope, "Screen Space Decals in Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine", SIGGRAPH 2011 Advances in Real-Time Rendering (public course notes); IEC 61966-2-1 for the atlas decode (ADR-038) | Reconstruct world position from the depth buffer and the inverse view-projection, transform into the decal box, discard outside the unit cube, fade by `\|dot(normal, projection axis)\|`. Ferrite stays on the forward translucent pass (ADR-045), recorded into the frame's one encoder (ADR-037). The host binds a receiver (layer + world normal) and a scene-colour copy. Albedo texels are authored sRGB (`Rgba8UnormSrgb`); the composite is linear and encoded only for an `Rgba8Unorm` target. Native terrain writes that same receiver (layer 0, the heightfield normal from screen-footprint central differences) in `SharedPass::Receiver`, against the output-sized depth from `depth_for_output` (ADR-041). |
| VFX | Whiteout blend of a detail normal onto the receiver normal | [class: public-literature] Barré-Brisebois & Hill, "Blending in Detail" (2012), blog.selfshadow.com/publications/blending-in-detail | Both normals are expressed in the receiver's tangent frame (base `n1 = (0,0,1)`), then `normalize(n1.xy + n2.xy, n1.z * n2.z)` and rotated back to world. Re-implemented from the published formula. Before that blend, a normal-channel atlas texel treats luminance as a height (a dark texel is low): one-texel finite differences in decal UV, scaled by `normal_strength` and added along the decal's right/up axes, so a charred centre and a rut groove recess (same central-difference height normal as the terrain layer bake). |

Each survivor is one screen quad whose rectangle is the union of the 16 px tiles that contain it (`upload_visible_decals` reads `bin.tiles`). A box clipped by the near plane expands to the viewport so the union stays conservative. Not a clustered lighting shader. |

A search of gfx-rs/wgpu issues for "ArrayStride Workgroup" and "10684" found no issue for the Workgroup storage class. naga 30.0.1 `back::spv` always emits `ArrayStride` and does not enable `WorkgroupMemoryExplicitLayoutKHR`. wgpu-hal 30.0.1 drops message id `0xb210f7c2` | Plain workgroup arrays stay. `shader_check` allowlists exactly `VUID-StandaloneSpirv-None-10684` from `spirv-val` (no other VUID) and the layout scan reports a Workgroup hit as a warning (ADR-135). The celestial sphere is hidden behind the planet. The moonlit air glow is in front of the surface (it is the air on the way down) and stars are not | [class: public-literature] Hillaire, EGSR 2020 (the sky-view LUT is the air; the surface is the march boundary); Bruneton, EG 2017 (ray–sphere intersection and transmittance to the ground); Lambert, *Photometria*, 1760 | `build_sky_view` alpha, `sample_sky`, `ground_radiance`, `physical_sky` / `night_air` in `outdoor_sky.wgsl`. | Render (clouds-depth) | Ray/sphere shell. `length(o)² − r²` is expanded about the planet radius (`horizontal² + 2·planet·(eye height − shell altitude) + eye height² − shell altitude²`) so f32 never squares a multi-megametre length, then the stable quadratic root `q = −(b + sign(b) * sqrt(disc))`, with roots `q` and `c / q` | [class: public-literature] Haines, Günther and Akenine-Möller, "Precision Improvements for Ray/Sphere Intersection", Ray Tracing Gems ch. 7 (Apress, 2019, open access). The product `(length(o) − r) * (length(o) + r)` still loses the half-metre ulp of `length(o)` and that becomes ~10 m on a long chord, so the coefficient is expanded before it is evaluated | `shell` in `clouds.wgsl`, `ferrite_render::clouds::shell_intersections` (f32, tested against the same expression in f64) |
| Render (clouds-depth) | View march: big step is four times the small step; a cheap-density hit returns to the start of that big step and walks small; eight empty small steps return to the big step. Outside the layer the small step is a fraction of the shell span over the step budget, growing with distance (`mix(0.35, 1.8, u²)`), floored at 4 m. Inside the layer it starts at 20 m and grows as a geometric series so the step budget sums to the segment (the 45 km fade times 1.5, 67.5 km, finishes in 64 steps). A camera inside cloud integrates one 20 m segment at the eye so the first step is not black | [class: public-literature] Schneider, "The Real-Time Volumetric Cloudscapes of Horizon: Zero Dawn", SIGGRAPH 2015 (large step, refine on a hit, step size increasing with distance). The 4× ratio, the eight-empty return, the 20 m near cap and the geometric schedule are Ferrite's | `march` / `small_step` in `clouds.wgsl`, `cloud_small_step` |
| Render (clouds-depth) | Depth-aware upsample of the half-resolution march. Each low-resolution texel stores the transmittance-weighted mean scatter distance and the scene distance of its footprint centre (metres, sky sentinel 60 km, half-float). The full-resolution pixel blends the 2×2 neighbours that tie the closest scene distance (bilinear weights), so a flat sky does not pick a single neighbour; a nearer depth wins alone. The sample is dropped when the cloud is behind the pixel by more than `max(32 m, 2% of the surface distance)`. The march clamps to the farthest real surface in the footprint; sky does not shorten the shell (the 60 km value is only the stored sentinel, because a grazing ray enters the layer past it). The footprint is up to 4×4 depth loads because the Hi-Z pyramid is max-only and is not built when GPU cull is off. View rays use the unjittered inverse; depth unprojection stays on the jittered inverse | [class: public-literature] Shopf, "Mixed Resolution Rendering", GDC 2009 (public; depth-aware upsample of a low-resolution effect). The weighted-mean scatter distance is the channel a later temporal reprojection can reproject | `fs_cloud_march` / `fs_cloud_composite` in `clouds.wgsl`; `CloudGpu::ray_from_clip` |
| Render (clouds-temporal) | Temporal cloud reconstruction: one texel of every 4×4 block marched per frame in 4×4 Bayer order, the other 15 reprojected from the previous frame along the texel's scatter distance with the previous unjittered view-projection (wind drift removed), clamped to the min/max of the 3×3 freshly marched texels, and replaced by the depth-matched fresh neighbour off screen or on a disocclusion; a camera cut marches every texel | [class: public-literature] Schneider, "The Real-Time Volumetric Cloudscapes of Horizon: Zero Dawn", SIGGRAPH 2015 Advances (1/16 of the pixels per frame, reprojection of the rest); Hillaire, "Physically Based Sky, Atmosphere and Cloud Rendering in Frostbite", SIGGRAPH 2016 course (4×4 update pattern, reprojection, fallback to the new low-resolution value); Bauer, "Creating the Atmospheric World of Red Dead Redemption 2", SIGGRAPH 2019 Advances (reprojected clouds with neighbourhood clamping); Karis, "High Quality Temporal Supersampling", SIGGRAPH 2014 (neighbourhood min/max clamp); Bayer, "An optimum method for two-level rendition of continuous-tone pictures", IEEE ICC 1973 (ordered-dither matrix) | `fs_cloud_fresh` / `fs_cloud_reconstruct` in `clouds.wgsl`, `cloud_bayer_offset` / `cloud_fresh_texel` in `ferrite_render::clouds`, `OutdoorState::draw_clouds`. The half-and-half blend of the marched texel, the wind-drift removal, the `max(32 m, 10 %)` disocclusion test and the depth-matched dilation are Ferrite's |
| Render (clouds-temporal) | Catmull-Rom history fetch as nine bilinear taps (the two middle weights per axis merged into one tap at `w2 / (w1 + w2)`) | [class: public-literature] Catmull & Rom, "A class of local interpolating splines", 1974 (the spline); the bilinear-tap factorisation as described publicly by Jimenez et al., "Filmic SMAA", SIGGRAPH 2016 Advances, and Pettineo, "Bicubic B-Spline and Catmull-Rom filtering" (MJP blog, 2016) | `history_catmull_rom` in `clouds.wgsl`. Tap coordinates are clamped to the inner half texel because the shared outdoor sampler repeats |

Variance is at least 0.008 m², so a one-ray cell is not a step function (a wall 17 cm past that ray stayed visible; a receiver a metre past the mean does not). A weight below 0.15 is dropped before the weights are normalised, so one barely-visible occluded probe cannot brighten the whole sample. Interior traces use 128 rays so a 45° cell is not a handful of ceiling hits | [class: public-literature] Donnelly & Lauritzen, "Variance Shadow Maps", I3D 2006 (Chebyshev; a tiny variance is a step), as used by Majercik et al. 2019 (they bilinear-filter the octahedral depth). Portals are the start (degenerate), each shared edge oriented so the left endpoint is on the walker's left in XZ (standard cross, independent of the area sign), then the goal (degenerate). `triarea2(a,b,c) = (c.x−a.x)*(b.z−a.z) − (b.x−a.x)*(c.z−a.z)` — Mononen's sign, positive on a right turn. The right edge tightens when `triarea2(apex, right, newRight) <= 0` and the new point is still strictly right of the left edge; otherwise the left point is emitted and the scan restarts at `apexIndex+1` (re-scanning the apex portal re-opens the opposite edge and the next portal restarts on the same apex, which grows without bound). Penumbra texels = normalised blocker gap × (source radius × depth extent / world texel), source radius 45 cm. The blocker search covers 16 texels; the filter radius clamps to 2.5..=10 (a 1-texel floor was a hard contact, and 18 texels washed the umbra into the lit pool). | Animation (pose search) | Offline motion-matching database: per-frame root-relative joint positions and finite-difference velocities, future root offset and relative yaw, per-channel mean/standard-deviation normalisation then weights, squared Euclidean nearest neighbour by brute force and by a median KD-tree that must agree (lowest index on ties). Playback keeps the current clip unless a same-clip candidate is strictly cheaper by more than a threshold; the chosen `(clip, time)` starts the existing inertializer. Looping trajectories extend past the clip end by composing each lap with the measured end-to-start transform — the local phase rotates about the lap-start position by the accumulated cycle yaw and each lap's displacement is added already turned — so a turning loop's second lap follows the turned arc (rescue-review fix, ADR-4869) | [class: public-literature] Simon Clavet, "Motion Matching and The Road to Next-Gen Animation", GDC 2016 (public talk: pose and trajectory features, nearest neighbour, bias to keep playing); Daniel Holden, Oussama Kanoun, Maksym Perepichka, Tiberiu Popa, "Learned Motion Matching", SIGGRAPH 2020 (feature sets and normalisation, paper only); Jon Louis Bentley, "Multidimensional Binary Search Trees Used for Associative Searching", CACM 18(9), 1975 (the KD-tree). | Nav / tile cache (v0.1.28, ADR-1484) | Navmesh tile cache: the walkable cell grid is kept after voxelisation and cut into square tiles; temporary obstacles (upright cylinders, axis-aligned boxes) are recorded with the tiles their radius-inflated footprint touches; an update rebuilds only queued tiles (restore cells, remove cells under touching obstacles, polygonise the tile) and stitches the tiles into one mesh, linking polygons across tile borders | [class: permissive-code; license: Zlib] **Ported** from Recast & Detour `DetourTileCache/Source/DetourTileCache.cpp` (obstacle requests, touched-tile lists, cylinder/box bounds), commit 9f4ce64458, Copyright (c) 2009-2010 Mikko Mononen, zlib licence (github.com/recastnavigation/recastnavigation) | `regia_nav::tile_cache`. Rewritten structure; the surface walk is a Cyrus-Beck exit-edge walk across portals (Cyrus & Beck 1978) instead of Detour's polygon search; neighbours come from a per-step uniform grid; collision resolution is Jacobi over all contacts (not only the 6 nearest); separation clamps by speed, not speed squared |

Original code. The dihedral gradient is re-derived from the normalized cross products (checked against finite differences in a unit test) and written in a form that stays finite at a flat hinge; flat rest angle is 0 by orienting the second normal; rope bending is a skip-one distance link; friction limit is `mu × normal correction / h` |
| Physics / convex decomposition (v0.1.28, ADR-1477) | Approximate convex decomposition of a triangle mesh: solid voxel grid (triangle/box overlap for surface cells, flood fill from the padding for the outside, voxel centers on the mesh bounds), best-first cutting of the most concave part by the axis-aligned cell-boundary plane that minimizes the summed concavity (hull volume minus solid volume) of the two sides plus a balance bias and a long-axis bias (own form of V-HACD's balance/symmetry idea), searched coarse to fine; plane costs from the hull of each side's voxel corners (per grid line the lowest and highest corner, corners on or behind their neighbors' midpoint dropped); part hulls from the mesh polygons clipped to the part's box plus the box corners inside the solid; greedy pairwise merge by added hull volume to `max_hulls` and below the concavity threshold | [class: public-literature] K. Mamou, F. Ghorbel, "A simple and efficient approach for 3D mesh approximate convex decomposition", IEEE ICIP 2009; the public V-HACD project description (K. Mamou, BSD-3; ideas only: voxelize, cut by planes that minimize concavity, merge hulls; no code read); I. E. Sutherland, G. W. Hodgman, "Reentrant polygon clipping", CACM 17(1), 1974 | `regia_physics::convex_decomposition` (`decompose`, `compound_shape`), `convex_decomposition/voxels.rs`. Original code. | Asset pipeline / alpha-tested voxelization of masked geometry (ADR-3108) | A masked triangle is split into a regular barycentric subdivision of sub-triangles no longer than half a voxel, each sampled at the centroids of its own regular subdivision (stratified sampling, each sample an equal share of the area; the masked raster's alpha test at each sample: bilinear texel alpha × base color alpha × vertex alpha against the cutoff). A voxel takes covered area where its samples pass and geometric area for all of them; fully covered triangles take the opaque path unchanged, fully cut-away ones make no voxel. Monte Carlo area estimation by stratified sampling (e.g. M. Pharr, W. Jakob, G. Humphreys, *Physically Based Rendering*, 3rd ed., 2016, § 13.8 "Stratified sampling"); the alpha test as glTF 2.0 `alphaMode: MASK` defines it (Khronos glTF 2.0 specification § 3.9.4) | [class: regia-design] Original code |  |

Monsi and T. Saeki, 1953; the projection function G: J. Ross, *The Radiation Regime and Architecture of Plant Stands*, 1981). With nothing cut away `f` = 1 and the rule is ADR-2445's opaque one. Ericson, *Real-Time Collision Detection*, 2005, § 5.1.5) and keeps the smaller of that and the analytic bound of ADR-2655 per voxel, the largest per level. | Asset pipeline / alpha-tested voxelization of masked geometry (ADR-3108) | A masked triangle is split into a regular barycentric subdivision of sub-triangles no longer than half a voxel, each sampled at the centroids of its own regular subdivision (stratified sampling, each sample an equal share of the area; the masked raster's alpha test at each sample: bilinear texel alpha × base color alpha × vertex alpha against the cutoff). Monsi and T. Saeki, 1953; the projection function G: J. Ross, *The Radiation Regime and Architecture of Plant Stands*, 1981). With nothing cut away `f` = 1 and the rule is ADR-2445's opaque one. Ericson, *Real-Time Collision Detection*, 2005, § 5.1.5) and keeps the smaller of that and the analytic bound of ADR-2655 per voxel, the largest per level. ## Source declarations (ADR-4581)

Each Source cell begins with one primary `[class: …]` declaration; mixed rows retain all
their citations. Classes and counts are explained in
[the cleanroom record status](01-cleanroom.md#provenance-record-status).
`cargo xtask check-provenance` checks every row.
| Fluid / GPU 64-bit fixed-point sums from 32-bit atomics (`fluid_flip.wgsl` `acc_add`/`acc_load`, ADR-4963) | A 64-bit two's-complement sum kept as a (low, high) pair of `atomic<u32>`: the low word takes the term with a wrapping add, the high word takes the term's sign extension plus the carry out of the low word, detected from the value the low word held before the add (`old + x < old`); integer adds commute, so the sum is exact and order-free. Read back exactly when it fits `i32`, else as `f32(hi) * 2^32 + f32(lo & 0xffff0000) + f32(lo & 0xffff)` | [class: public-literature] Multi-word (multiple-precision) addition with carry, D. Knuth, *The Art of Computer Programming* vol. 2, § 4.3.1 Algorithm A (textbook); WGSL specification (atomic built-ins return the previous value, integer atomics wrap) | Original WGSL code |

Each component is an unsigned biased 16-bit value (`round(clamp(v,-1,1)*32767)+32767`) in the low half of a priority word. Dispatch one publishes every X word with `atomicMax`. Dispatch two, after that max is visible, publishes the Y word only for entries whose X word equals the stored max. The stored pair is the lexicographic maximum, so it is one of the inputs. A signed low half would make the greater unsigned word the more negative component. A shader spinlock is not used: invocations in one subgroup have no independent forward progress, and a bilinear splat contends inside a subgroup. | [class: standard] WGSL specification, atomic read-modify-write built-ins (`atomicMax` is associative and commutative); Vulkan specification, "Limited Forward Progress" (shader invocations are not required to make independent forward progress). | Procgen / cellular noise F1 and F2 − F1 (ADR-7280; `regia_gen::noise`) | One hashed, jittered feature point per cell; nearest and second-nearest squared distance over the 3 × 3 neighbourhood; output `sqrt(F1)` or `sqrt(F2) − sqrt(F1)` capped at 1 | [class: public-literature] S. Worley, "A Cellular Texture Basis Function", SIGGRAPH 1996 | Original code |
| Procgen / box blur cascade and image masks (ADR-7280; `regia_gen::masks`) | Separable box blur repeated `passes` times (three approximate a Gaussian), wrap or clamp edges, `f64` sums in fixed order; threshold with smoothstep band; levels with gamma by `regia_core::math::det::det_powf`; blend modes multiply/screen/overlay/add/subtract/min/max/mix | [class: public-literature] W. M. Wells, "Efficient Synthesis of Gaussian Filters by Cascaded Uniform Filters", IEEE PAMI 8(2), 1986; blend-mode formulas from the W3C "Compositing and Blending Level 1" specification (public) | Original code |
| Procgen / edge and cavity masks from dihedral angles baked into UV space (ADR-7280; `regia_gen::curvature_masks`) | Welded edges shared by two faces: bend `1 − n₁·n₂` ramped between two angles (cosines from `regia_core::math::det::cos`), convex when the second face's far corner lies below the first face's plane; triangles rasterized in UV with barycentric edge functions at texel centres, world point to segment distance with a smoothstep falloff over the feature edges at the triangle's corners, max-combined (order independent); 4-neighbour dilation rings | [class: public-literature] Dihedral angle and sharp-edge detection in M. Botsch et al., "Polygon Mesh Processing" (AK Peters, 2010); half-space triangle rasterization by edge functions, J. Pineda, "A Parallel Algorithm for Polygon Rasterization", SIGGRAPH 1988 | Original code |
| Procgen / thermal erosion on a heightfield (ADR-7280; `regia_gen::Heightfield::thermal_erode`) | Per pass, each sample compares itself with its 8 neighbours; drops steeper than `talus · distance` share `rate · (largest excess)` in proportion to their excess; transfers from the pass's starting heights accumulated in an `f64` buffer and applied together (order independent, conserving), closed borders | [class: public-literature] F. K. Musgrave, C. E. Kolb, R. S. Mace, "The Synthesis and Rendering of Eroded Fractal Terrains", SIGGRAPH 1989; J. Olsen, "Realtime Procedural Terrain Generation" (2004, public PDF) | Original code |
| Procgen / heightfield terrace, pad, slope and normal maps, terrain export (ADR-7280; `regia_gen::Heightfield`) | Terrace by quantizing the normalized height into `steps` levels; pad by distance with a smoothstep band; slope and normals by central differences (one-sided at borders); terrain export as 16-bit samples over `[min, max]` with scale and offset in `mesh_from_heightfield`'s layout | [class: public-literature] Textbook height-map processing (central differences, quantization; e.g. "Texturing and Modeling: A Procedural Approach", terrain chapters) | Original code |
| Networking / join window: join-critical spawns outside the spawn budget, and the dev protocol-type diff (ADR-7212; `regia_net::replication` pack, `session::travel`, `session::lifecycle::{protocol_types_line, explain_protocol_mismatch}`; lane post05-net-session-lifecycle) | While a connection has not yet received every spawn it owns or whose profile is `sent_to_all`, those candidates rank as forced and the packer lets forced spawns past the per-tick spawn count (bytes still charged); the window closes when none is pending and reopens at a travel. Protocol mismatch: the dev server lists `type path = 32-bit fingerprint` of each registered type (a hash of the fields the protocol hash already covers), the dev client diffs the list against its own by name | [class: regia-design] Regia spec 77 §§ 4, 6.1 and spec 72 §§ 6-7 (the spawn budget and forced records this extends); no outside source | Original Rust |
| Networking / travel keep list: a client drops the old level's copies at `TravelBegin` (ADR-7259; `regia_net::session::travel::{travel_keep_for, drop_copies_for_travel}`, `replication::client_drop_for_travel`; lane post05w3-net-travel-mods) | In the step that despawns the old level, the server reads the `NetId`s of its persistent replicated entities and its next unassigned `NetId` (a watermark: ids are never reused); `TravelBegin` carries both, and the client despawns every copy below the watermark that is not in the list, on the state channel tombstoning the id past every tick so in-flight frames cannot revive it; copies at or above the watermark (the new level) are untouched | [class: regia-design] Regia spec 77 § 6.2 and spec 71 § 4.1 (`NetId`s never reused); no outside source | Original Rust |
| Networking / travel tombstones on the reliable tick stream (ADR-7295; `regia_net::replication::{client_apply_state, despawn_copies}`, `replication::state_channel::ClientStateChannel::{begin_travel_floor, clear_travel_tombstone, is_tombstoned}`, `session::travel::drop_copies_for_travel`; lane post05w4-net-travel-tombstone-k) | A travel's `TravelBegin` is a session message and overtakes the replication stream, so on protocol 1 the client installs a floor: every `NetId` below the `TravelKeep.below` watermark the travel named is old level (ids are never reused), and spawn/update records of a covered id in flight are dropped and counted whatever their tick; the persistent ids and the ids the server's despawn records reached are exempt, the latter exactly where the state channel's point tombstone is replaced by the notice | [class: regia-design] Regia spec 77 § 6.2 and spec 71 § 4.1 (`NetId`s never reused); no outside source | Original Rust |

The plain wire's control points are the pins and the pins moved a frame level outward (`min(30, distance / 6)`), the curve the canvas asks egui-snarl 0.12 (MIT OR Apache-2.0) to draw with its public `SnarlStyle` fields (`wire_style: Bezier3`, `wire_frame_size`, `downscale_wire_frame`) | [class: public-literature] P. de Casteljau's subdivision and the convex-hull property of Bézier curves: G. Riesenfeld, "A Theoretical Development for the Computer Generation and Display of Piecewise Polynomial Surfaces", IEEE TPAMI 2(1), 1980 | Original code; the curve's frame rule was read from egui-snarl's public source to match what it draws, no code copied |

| Editor / gizmo reference spaces and surface snap (ADR-7756; `regia_editor::viewport_ops::{space_basis, to_world, to_parent, delta_in_parent}`, `surface_tools::{surface_at, surface_snap_pose}`; lane w12-viewport-gizmo-snap) | Change of basis for a rigid step: a step given along a basis `B` is `B·t` in world, `B·r·B⁻¹` as a world rotation, and `P⁻¹` of those in the parent's space (rotation `Rp⁻¹·R·Rp`); poses compose as decomposed scale, rotation, translation. Surface snap is a view-ray cast against the drawn meshes and terrain with the moved subtrees excluded, the hit lifted along the face normal turned toward the camera, and the up axis aligned by the shortest arc (`Quat::from_rotation_arc`). | [class: public-literature] Standard linear algebra: Akenine-Möller et al., *Real-Time Rendering*, 4th ed., ch. 4 | Original code. |
| Editor / Inspector property search and Modified only (lane w12-inspector-panel, spec addendum § 7.1; `regia_editor::inspector::{search, defaults}`) | Fields are matched with the existing `regia_ui::fuzzy::fuzzy_match` (ADR-1842) against three candidates in turn: the display name, the reflect path, then `"<Component> <field>"`, where the last counts only if at least one matched character falls in the field part (so letters found only in the component name never match every field). The visible rows are a set of hit reflect paths plus their ancestors and descendants (string prefix at a `.` or `[` boundary); Modified only is the set of leaves whose `PartialReflect::reflect_partial_eq` against the baseline (the prefab template's component, else the type's reflected `Default`) is not `Some(true)`, walking struct and tuple-struct fields (with no baseline every leaf counts as changed). | [class: regia-design] Own design over `regia_ui::fuzzy::fuzzy_match` (ADR-1842) and `PartialReflect::reflect_partial_eq` | Original code; no outside source. |
| Editor / main window placement (ADR-7753; lane w12-layouts-workspaces) | `regia_editor::window_state::place`: the saved monitor by name, else the primary display, else the first; size clamped to the monitor; the saved position kept only on the same monitor and only when at least 64 px of each axis stays on it, else centered | [class: regia-design] No outside source; plain rectangle arithmetic | Original Rust; about 40 lines |
